supportedContexts: bare value (the PMAK- prefix is the only marker; no keyword required)
lowercase-hex segments only (uppercase hex is outside the benchmark claim)
value on the line after an unrelated comment line (CRLF)
empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Postman's docs state no PMAK- grammar (only the X-API-Key header and a postman-api-key variable). Its own Insights Agent redaction config fixes PMAK- + 24 lowercase hex + '-' + 34 lowercase hex, matching gitleaks and Nosey Parker, while trufflehog corroborates only the prefix and 59-byte width. The same Postman config also redacts a bare PMAK- + 24 hex value (L32). That pattern matches the id part of every full key, so the family reads it as a prefix-level scrub and keeps the 24-hex fragment as a non-credential near miss (settled by L72, a judgement). The benchmark claims only lowercase-hex keys. No issued key has been measured, and a second Postman credential (PMAT-) exists outside the contract (redact-secret#700).

empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Twilio documents no alphabet. Its own code checks only the length (32), and one Twilio sample accepts [a-z0-9], so lowercase hex rests on scanner rules.
